map_note.t: Alabama is using the 2023 Legislature-drawn map (one majority-Black district, AL-07), not the court-ordered map used in 2024. After the Supreme Court decided Louisiana v. Callais in April 2026, which narrowed Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act, the Court lifted the Milligan injunctions on May 11. A district court blocked the map again on May 26, and on June 2 the Supreme Court stayed that order 6–3. The Legislature nullified the May 19 primaries in AL-01, 02, 06 and 07 and held winner-take-all special primaries there on Aug 11, 2026; AL-03, 04 and 05 kept the May 19 primary and June 16 runoff.

AL-01.note: Open seat. Under the reinstated 2023 legislative map, AL-01 is Mobile and Baldwin counties plus Escambia and Covington. The May 19 GOP primary (Carl 40.3%, Marques 31.1%) was nullified; in the Aug 11, 2026 winner-take-all special primary (no runoff) Jerry Carl won ~74.7% over Austin Sidwell, John Mills and Lucas Burger. Clyde Jones Jr. was the only Democrat to qualify.

AL-02.note: Most competitive Alabama race. The reinstated 2023 map moves AL-02 to the Wiregrass, Montgomery and the eastern Black Belt; Black voting-age population falls from 48.7% (court map Figures won under in 2024) to 39.9%. Figures was unopposed; Rhett Marques won the Aug 11 six-way GOP special primary with ~50% (Hampton Harris ~21.6%, David Matthews ~17.4%).
